column1: # Known --posix divergences that are NOT Bash++ leaks.
# EMPTY, and that is the point: there are currently no known cert-owned
# divergences. Every shape in the corpus parses identically under --posix in
# the engine and in real bash 5.3.
# It held five entries — the command-position NAME[...] defect, where a word
# like f[[]int] or f[*T] was rejected by the engine and accepted by bash 5.3
# because the subscript was parsed as arithmetic. Fixed in sh f091034a
# ("syntax: recover naked bracket words at assignment boundary"), and the gate
# then FAILED with five STALE lines demanding these rows be removed. That is
# the ratchet working: an allowlist that only ever loosens is a hole, so a fix
# Add a row here ONLY for a divergence owned by another workstream, with its
# owner named. The gate prints every entry on every run — an allowlist, never a
# silence — and fails when a listed id stops diverging.
